results.reason: Issue 1 says the 10-Business-Day window from the September 14 First Schedule Supplement has expired. It explains that under §5.7(c) the Ferrovane non-renewal is deemed cured for Article IX and the §7.2(a) bring-down, so Buyer has lost both its walk right and its indemnity.

The escrow discussion covers only housekeeping and tax treatment. It never notes that the Escrow Agreement's narrower 'Losses' definition (out-of-pocket only, excluding diminution in value, lost profits or fees) controls escrow disbursement under §11.11.

Issue 2 says MSA §14.2 treats a >50% acquisition as an assignment requiring consent and that the 100% share sale triggers it. It notes the consent is not in Annex 7.2(d) or the §7.2(d) condition, so Buyer could have to close and then face termination or repricing by its sole-source supplier.
The memo counts 10 Business Days from September 14 and concludes the window closed September 28, 2026, before the October 13 letter.
The memo states the escrow amount is $4,850,000.
The document is a memorandum addressed to the Supervising Attorney. Each issue has 'Where it appears', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Section III is headed 'Open Points: Not Resolvable from the Documents / Client Input Needed'.
The memo expressly says Harrowgate has no remaining right to terminate over Ferrovane and advises against implying a live termination right.
The memo states Annex 7.2(d) lists only the Lender Payoff Letter and the Lien release, and that the Tavinor consent is not a closing condition.
